title: Composable Minimal Endpoint Suite PRD and Launch Checklist
creator: Asha Mehta
description: Objective: ship a small, composable set of hosted API endpoints (CompactChat, TextCompleteLite, VectorEmbedFast, RerankLight) that developers can combine client-side to build chat/completion/embedding/rerank flows with predictable latency and cost. This PRD defines contract stability, minimal payload shapes, required server-side features (structured output, deterministic error codes, KV prefix caching compatibility), and an actionable launch checklist focused on developer ergonomics and operational readiness.
goals: Provide a minimal API surface that can be composed to cover 80% of customer inference use cases while reducing per-token cost by enabling smaller fixed overheads
Guarantee contract stability for 3 months post-launch (schema + error codes) with upgrade paths and deprecation notices
Deliver observability and SLOs sufficient for enterprise onboarding (latency P95, error budget, token cost telemetry)
Make SDK and Console updates so developers can discover composable patterns and measure unit economics
non_goals: Not building a new multi-turn state store; composability assumes client-managed context stitching
Not replacing full-featured chat endpoint; this suite is intentionally minimal and predictable
Not adding multimodal inputs for this initial launch
scope: In-scope: API contracts, minimal required server-side features (structured JSON output, deterministic failure states, prefix KV cache compatibility), SDK helpers, console signup and cost views, docs and code samples, basic canary rollout. Out-of-scope: advanced rollout automation, region-by-region pricing differentiation, on-prem/private packaging for this tranche.
requirements: CompactChat endpoint accepts a minimal prompt+instructions payload and returns streaming tokens and a final structured metadata block
TextCompleteLite supports stop sequences, temperature, top_p and max_tokens; returns per-token timestamps for latency attribution
VectorEmbedFast returns 1024/1536-dimensional embeddings with deterministic normalization and optional batch endpoint
RerankLight accepts a list of candidate texts and a query and returns stable score floats in a documented range plus tie-breaker heuristics
All endpoints must include a stable error schema (error.code, error.type, error.message) and mapping doc
All endpoints must opt into the KV prefix cache contract so SDKs can enable prefix caching when model and route are compatible
Rate limiting behavior must be defined per endpoint and surfaced via headers
Telemetry hooks: token_count, model_variant, latency_ms, cache_hit boolean exposed to console and logs
acceptance_criteria: API contract documented with examples for JSON and streaming responses and signed off by API review
Schema tests in CI that verify response fields, error codes, and streaming semantics
Performance gate: cold-start P95 < 300ms for CompactChat 1k token requests on target hardware; sustained throughput linear scaling tests pass
Cost gate: median per-token CPU/GPU unit cost measured and within 15% of forecast for default configuration
SDKs (JS/Python) provide helper composition functions and pass end-to-end integration tests with mock orchestration
Console: a dedicated composable endpoints page with cost-per-token estimator and example recipes
Security: threat model reviewed and KMS-integrations validated for hosted mode
Rollout plan approved with canary criteria and fallback policy
open_questions: Should CompactChat include server-side support for short-lived conversation IDs for easier client stitching?
What is the acceptable minimum embedding dimension for VectorEmbedFast to balance cost and downstream quality?
Do we require a standard client-side library for composition patterns or just SDK helpers?
How aggressive should default rate limits be for public preview vs GA?
scope_changes_and_decisions: 2026-01-08: Decision to keep conversation state client-managed to reduce server complexity (approved by Eng lead)
2026-02-02: Reduced embedding dims option postponed to post-GA after product telemetry indicates demand
2026-03-01: Added explicit telemetry fields (cache_hit, model_variant) following privacy review recommendations
rollout_plan: Phase 0: internal dogfood + infra canary (2 weeks) -> Phase 1: invited beta with SDK support and paid preview (4 weeks) -> Phase 2: staged regional GA with pricing announcement and enterprise enablement (3 weeks). Canary success criteria: error rate < 0.5%, latency regressions < 10% vs baseline, token cost within forecast.
launch_checklist: API surface: publish OpenAPI + streaming examples and schema docs
SDKs: ship JS/Python helpers and snippets, update changelogs
Console: add composable endpoints page and cost estimator widgets
Docs: quickstarts for common composition patterns (chat+rerank, search+embed+rerank)
Observability: dashboards for token volume, P95 latency, error rates, cache hit rate
Security: complete security review, KMS test, and audit logging enabled for hosted preview
Performance: run full perf suite and attach baseline artifacts to ticket
Testing: e2e smoke tests, contract tests, chaos test simulating partial region outage
Billing: update pricing table and billing events for new endpoints
Support: prepare KB articles and playbook for common troubleshooting
Legal/Compliance: update terms for hosted API changes where needed
Canary: plan and rollback instructions documented with GitHub PR references
test_plan: Unit: schema and input validation tests for each endpoint
Integration: SDK+API e2e tests mocking real composition flows
Perf: P50/P95/P99 latency and throughput sweeps for key payload sizes
Regression: ensure chat feature parity for critical params with full chat endpoint
Chaos: degrade a dependent service (KV cache) and validate graceful fallback
metrics: Cache hit ratio for compatible routes
Adoption: number of unique API keys calling composable endpoints
Conversion: percent of beta customers moving to paid Dedicated or GA tiers
stakeholders: Eng leads: Liam Carter (runtime), Priya Singh (infra)
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Clients misuse composition and create inefficient call patterns -> Mitigation: publish recommended patterns and provide SDK helpers that batch calls
Risk: Observability gaps across composed flows -> Mitigation: add correlation IDs and token-level telemetry and update dashboards
Risk: Contract rigidity causes breaking changes -> Mitigation: guarantee 3-month freeze and provide deprecation window + migration guide
Risk: Unexpected cost behavior for small customers -> Mitigation: add cost-per-call estimator in Console and default safer rate-limits for new accounts
notes: This approach aims to trade some convenience for predictability and lower overhead in the common case. Expect follow-up tickets for advanced composition server-side helpers if adoption is strong.
Coordinate with Dedicated and Private teams early to ensure later parity for enterprise customers.
Plan for a 1:1 launch support duty rotation for the first two weeks after GA.
